Core memory
KOR MEM-uh-ree
noun (Gen-Z slang)
From Pixar’s Inside Out (2015), in which a girl’s most important experiences are stored as glowing core memories that power the "islands" of her personality. Around 2021–2022 TikTok made "that unlocked a core memory" a stock phrase for a sight, song, or smell that brings back a formative childhood moment, and "making core memories" a caption for family outings. The sequel Inside Out 2 (2024) renewed the phrase.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

In current slang a core memory is a formative memory — the kind that shaped who you are — and "that unlocked a core memory" means something suddenly brought one back. Parents now speak of "making core memories" with their children, and the instinct is right. The Christian observation: God builds His people by memory on purpose. Israel was commanded, "thou shalt remember all the way which the LORD thy God led thee these forty years in the wilderness" (Deu 8:2), and the stones taken from the Jordan were to "be for a memorial unto the children of Israel for ever" (Jos 4:7). The psalmist preaches to his own forgetful heart: "Bless the LORD, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits" (Psa 103:2). Jeremiah, sitting in the ruins of Jerusalem, survives by memory: "This I recall to my mind, therefore have I hope" (Lam 3:21). And the Lord Jesus gave His church a meal that is a core memory by design: "this do in remembrance of me" (Luk 22:19). The Christian does not leave core memories to chance, or to a cartoon of emotions at a control panel. A father tells his daughter: we will make memories, and the deepest ones will be of God’s faithfulness — family worship, answered prayer, the Lord’s Table — so that when trouble comes, you have something to recall to mind.

Webster 1828 Definition

Gen-Z slang (from Pixar’s Inside Out, 2015; TikTok c. 2021–2022) for a formative memory — and God shapes His people by memory on purpose, from the Jordan stones to the Lord’s Supper.

expand to see more

CORE MEMORY, n. (Gen-Z slang, c. 2021–present; from Inside Out, 2015) A formative memory that helped shape who one is. "Grandpa teaching me to fish is a core memory."

"That unlocked a core memory" — something brought an old memory back vividly. "Making core memories" — doing something meant to be remembered.

Older, plain sense of memory: the faculty of recalling the past; a thing remembered; the name of the dead ("of blessed memory").

Webster (1828), root word memory: “MEM'ORY, noun [&hellip;] 1. The faculty of the mind by which it retains the knowledge of past events, or ideas which are past. A distinction is made between memory and recollection. memory retains past ideas without any, or with little effort; recollection implies an effort to recall ideas that are past. Memory is the purveyor of reason.”

Decode for parents: your children are telling you which moments formed them. Fill the album with God’s faithfulness.

Key Scripture

Deu 8:2 — "And thou shalt remember all the way which the LORD thy God led thee these forty years in the wilderness, to humble thee, and to prove thee, to know what was in thine heart, whether thou wouldest keep his commandments, or no."

Jos 4:7 — "Then ye shall answer them, That the waters of Jordan were cut off before the ark of the covenant of the LORD; when it passed over Jordan, the waters of Jordan were cut off: and these stones shall be for a memorial unto the children of Israel for ever."

Psa 103:2 — "Bless the LORD, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits:"

Lam 3:21 — "This I recall to my mind, therefore have I hope."

Luk 22:19 — "And he took bread, and gave thanks, and brake it, and gave unto them, saying, This is my body which is given for you: this do in remembrance of me."

Modern Corruption

Core memory rightly sees that memories form a person; the drift is a cartoon psychology that makes feelings the architects of the self, when Scripture makes remembering God’s works the foundation.

expand to see more

Inside Out taught a generation a picture of the soul: little emotions at a control panel, sorting memories into the islands of a personality. It is clever, and it is not the Bible’s picture. In Scripture the heart is not a committee of feelings but a moral centre that loves and trusts, and memory is a duty before it is a mood. God does not wait for a core memory to happen; He commands His people to set up memorials (Jos 4:7), rehearse His works (Deu 8:2), and keep a feast in His remembrance (Luk 22:19).

So the phrase is worth keeping and filling. Families make core memories whether they intend to or not; the only question is what they are about. A childhood full of screens remembers screens. A childhood with psalms at bedtime, a father praying through a crisis, and the Lord’s Supper taken with reverence remembers a faithful God, and that memory holds under weight: "This I recall to my mind, therefore have I hope" (Lam 3:21). Teach your children to bless the LORD and forget not all His benefits (Psa 103:2).

Latin memoria (remembrance) → English memory → Pixar’s Inside Out (2015) → c. 2021–2022 TikTok: "that unlocked a core memory."

Latin memor — mindful; memoria, remembrance

c. 2021–2022 TikTok: "that unlocked a core memory," "making core memories"

Usage

""The smell of that church basement just unlocked a core memory.""

"Set up stones, and tell your children what they mean (Jos 4:7)."

"This do in remembrance of me (Luk 22:19) — the church’s core memory."
